title: The Operational Facilitator's alignment finding gates whether an Artifact amendment ever reaches a token holder vote
content:
Under A.6.1.1.5.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3, "Within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment." A.6.1.1.5.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 then makes the vote conditional: "**Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment** with the Sky Core Atlas and Obex Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll."

The ordering is the design. Token holders do not vote on whether a proposal is aligned; they vote only on proposals that have already been found aligned. A misalignment finding is therefore not an opinion entered into the debate — it is a terminal outcome, and the Facilitator's only further obligation is to "provide the reasoning for it" on the Forum.

This is Alignment Engineering applied to the amendment path: rather than trusting an electorate to reject misaligned changes, the design removes misaligned changes from the ballot. It lowers the alignment a holder needs in order for the system to produce aligned outcomes, at the direct cost of concentrating a veto in one role.

The checks on that veto are thin and social rather than structural. The Facilitator must publish reasoning, and must act within seven days, but no appeal, override, or supermajority bypass appears in the Routine Protocol. The aligned finding also carries a second component — confirming "that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize" — so the same actor judges both whether a change is permitted and whether it is buildable.
description: A proposal only proceeds to a Snapshot poll where the Facilitator's review finds alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Obex Artifact
